correctness.rationale: The full-gradient Armijo inequality is solved exactly for the maximal permissible step; the compressed objective difference is an exact quadratic identity. All 2D spectral orientations reduce to a positive ratio of two cosine functions. Its tangent-at-zero condition gives \(\kappa(r-1)^2=(\kappa-1)^2r\sin^2\theta\), and the top-one cone restricts \(\theta\le\pi/4\); these give the sharp global factor. Continuity handles strict top-one counterexamples; the critical-condition formula follows algebraically. Independent finite orientation and direct energy checks succeeded. No unproved implication about long-run stability is used.

value.rationale: The question is intrinsic to composing full-gradient line search with gradient communication sparsification. A provably maximal safe scaling and sharp full spectrum/eigenvector-angle boundary distinguish this from general sufficient convergence estimates: even a globally accepted full-gradient step can become non-descent after top-one compression. The golden-ratio-square half-Armijo threshold is a natural closed-form reliability benchmark, not an arbitrary finite-sample count.
